title: Named-root naming can deadlock: a pending transition must be retried first, but its exact retry is refused as stale
outcome: A session whose earlier naming request went stale can always name a root again through a supported path, without a restart and without losing the journal's protection against an unsettled transition.
acceptance: The failing sequence is reproduced by a deterministic test: a named-root transition pending for one root, its claim association going stale, then both the original request and a naming of another root
After the fix that sequence ends with a settled root by a supported call, the refusal text tells the caller what to do, and a transition that truly remains unsettled still can't be overtaken

completion.summary: A pending name whose claim was recovered no longer blocks naming: a read showing a newer fence settles it, under either refusal code, and the next naming finishes. Refusal text says what to do, and anything without that proof stays pending. Remaining wall from a host-raised end is filed as w-40747b1f243d.
